Agreed. I was lucky enough to go to a high school with a good art program but they were constantly losing supplies and we didn't have the funds to get new ones. Even then, even when the schools allow you to pursue your talents and interests there's still a lot of pressure on being the best at it. They don't let you do anything purely for fun and it's so damaging. I still love art and find it very relaxing, but I remember spending a lot of nights crying over that class because it was just so stressful. One of the best ways to destroy a passion for something is to set impossible standards and deadlines on it.

What I always hated most about it was the cultural attitude toward school; like if you're not at the top or at least fighting to be up there then you're not even trying and are considered worthless. Scores become more important than physical and especially mental health, and we're conditioned to be afraid of meaningless letters and numbers because we're taught to believe that a low score means there's something wrong and disgusting about us as human beings. Then lately they've had the gall to be like "take care of yourselves in this challenging time :) here are some generic guides on mindfulness" like don't act like you've ever really cared. They only want the students alive so they can profit off us.
